source.book: Indian Society

cards.subject: sociology

cards.subject: sociology

cards.back: Sociology tells you about what kinds of groups or groupings there are in society, what their relationships are to each other

cards.subject: sociology

cards.back: But all of these are about one person and derive meaning from this personalised perspective.
cards.quote: But all of these are about one person and derive meaning from this personalised perspective.

source.book: Indian Society

reasons: review:Blank 'personalised' has rivals (personal, individual); not an exam point.

cards.quote: We begin with a discussion of the demographic structure of the Indian population (Chapter 2).

source.book: Indian Society

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: In Chapter 3, we revisit the basic building blocks of Indian society in the form of the institutions of ____, ____ and ____.
cards.back: In Chapter 3, we revisit the basic building blocks of Indian society in the form of the institutions of caste, tribe and family.
cards.quote: In Chapter 3, we revisit the basic building blocks of Indian society in the form of the institutions of caste, tribe and family.

source.book: Indian Society

cards.subject: sociology

cards.quote: As a unique feature of the Indian subcontinent, caste has always attracted a lot of scholarly attention.

source.book: Indian Society

reasons: review:Preview filler, not a definition or exam fact.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Chapter 4 explores the socio-cultural dimensions of the ____ as a powerful institution that has been the vehicle of change throughout world history.
cards.back: Chapter 4 explores the socio-cultural dimensions of the market as a powerful institution that has been the vehicle of change throughout world history.
cards.quote: Chapter 4 explores the socio-cultural dimensions of the market as a powerful institution that has been the vehicle of change throughout world history.

source.book: Indian Society

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Given that the most sweeping and rapid economic changes were brought about first by ____ and then by ____

cards.quote: Given that the most sweeping and rapid economic changes were brought about first by colonialism and then by developmental policies

source.book: Indian Society

reasons: review:Roadmap filler; 'developmental policies' has rivals (planning, development); order of two blanks not fixed.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Among the features of our society that have been the cause of greatest concern are its seemingly unlimited capacity for generating ____ and ____.
cards.back: Among the features of our society that have been the cause of greatest concern are its seemingly unlimited capacity for generating inequality and exclusion.
cards.quote: Among the features of our society that have been the cause of greatest concern are its seemingly unlimited capacity for generating inequality and exclusion.

source.book: Indian Society

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Chapter 5 looks at inequality and exclusion in the context of ____, ____, ____ and the ‘disabled’.
cards.back: Chapter 5 looks at inequality and exclusion in the context of caste, tribe, gender and the ‘disabled’.
cards.quote: Chapter 5 looks at inequality and exclusion in the context of caste, tribe, gender and the ‘disabled’.

source.book: Indian Society

cards.subject: sociology

cards.back: Notorious as an instrument of division and injustice, the caste system has been the object of concerted attempts
cards.quote: Notorious as an instrument of division and injustice, the caste system has been the object of concerted attempts

source.book: Indian Society

reasons: review:Roadmap filler; both blanks have rivals (oppression, discrimination, exclusion).

cards.quote: the caste system has been the object of concerted attempts by the state and by the oppressed castes to reform or even abolish it.

cards.subject: sociology

cards.front: Between these two stages is a ____ stage of movement from a backward to an advanced stage
cards.back: Between these two stages is a transitional stage of movement from a backward to an advanced stage
cards.quote: Between these two stages is a transitional stage of movement from a backward to an advanced stage

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: The ____ (and last) stage is also one of low growth in a developed society
cards.back: The third (and last) stage is also one of low growth in a developed society
cards.quote: The third (and last) stage is also one of low growth in a developed society

source.book: Indian Society

reasons: review:Blank is only the ordinal 'third' (already implied by '(and last)'); no mark-carrying content. The stage idea is covered by cards 23/24.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Which was the single biggest epidemic in India, and how many did it kill?
cards.back: But the single biggest epidemic was the influenza epidemic of 1918-19, which killed as many as 170 lakh people, or about 5% of the total population of India at that time.
cards.quote: But the single biggest epidemic was the influenza epidemic of 1918-19, which killed as many as 170 lakh people, or about 5% of the total population of India at that time.

source.book: Indian Society
source.section: 2.2 Size and Growth of India's Population

reasons: review:NCERT gives three different death tolls for the 1918-19 influenza (12.5 million p12, 170 lakh p14, 17 million Box 2.2); 'how many did it kill' has no single right answer from the front.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: How many people is the ‘Spanish Flu’ of 1918–1919 thought to have killed worldwide?
cards.back: The most infamous pandemic was “Spanish Flu” which affected large parts of the world population and is thought to have killed at least 40 million people in 1918-1919.
cards.quote: The most infamous pandemic was “Spanish Flu” which affected large parts of the world population and is thought to have killed at least 40 million people in 1918-1919.

source.book: Indian Society
source.section: Box 2.2: The Global Influenza Pandemic of 1918–19

reasons: review:Box 2.2 global case detail ('at least 40 million'); same box also says 25 million in six months and up to 100 million; trivia, not CUET-worthy and not a stable single fact.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What was India’s crude birth rate (SRS 2020), and which states had the highest birth rate?
cards.back: According to Sample Registration System, Statistical report 2020, India’s crude birth rate was 19.5. The rural birth rate was 21.1 and urban birth rate was 16.1. As per this statistics, Bihar with 25.5 and Uttar Pradesh with 25.1 account for the highest birth rate in India.
cards.quote: According to Sample Registration System, Statistical report 2020, India’s crude birth rate was 19.5. The rural birth rate was 21.1 and urban birth rate was 16.1. As per this statistics, Bihar with 25.5 and Uttar Pradesh with 25.1 account for the highest birth rate in India.

source.book: Indian Society
source.section: 2.2 Size and Growth of India's Population

reasons: review:Bundle of SRS 2020 statistics (CBR 19.5, rural 21.1, urban 16.1, Bihar 25.5, UP 25.1); too number-heavy and perishable to be a memory card; compound front.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: How have the shares of the 15–59 and 60+ age groups changed over the same period?
cards.back: The share of the 15–59 age group has increased slightly from 53% to 63%, while the share of the 60+ age group is very small but it has begun to increase (from 5% to 7%) over the same period.
cards.quote: The share of the 15–59 age group has increased slightly from 53% to 63%, while the share of the 60+ age group is very small but it has begun to increase (from 5% to 7%) over the same period.

source.book: Indian Society
source.section: 2.3 Age Structure of the Indian Population

reasons: review:Front says 'over the same period' with no period stated (relies on previous card, 1971-2011). Also text gives 60+ as 7% in 2011 while Table 2 shows 8%.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: social scientists believe that the cause has to be sought in the ____ of girl babies

cards.quote: social scientists believe that the cause has to be sought in the differential treatment of girl babies

source.book: Indian Society

cards.front: What non-farm occupations are rural people increasingly engaged in?

cards.quote: Rural people are increasingly engaged in non-farm rural occupations like transport services, business enterprises or craft manufacturing.

source.book: Indian Society

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What goal for life expectancy at birth does National Health Policy 2017 set for 2025?

cards.quote: Increase Life Expectancy at birth from 67.5 to 70 by 2025.

source.book: Indian Society
source.section: Box 2.5: Important Goals of National Health Policy 2017

reasons: review:One of ~25 Box 2.5 health targets (life expectancy 67.5 to 70); isolated figure, trivia; also out of book order (p32 cards placed after p33).

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: the English word ‘caste’ is actually a borrowing from the ____ casta, meaning ____.
cards.back: the English word ‘caste’ is actually a borrowing from the Portuguese casta, meaning pure breed.
cards.quote: the English word ‘caste’ is actually a borrowing from the Portuguese casta, meaning pure breed.

source.book: Indian Society

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: It is only in the ____ period that caste became the rigid institution that is familiar to us from well known definitions.
cards.back: It is only in the post-Vedic period that caste became the rigid institution that is familiar to us from well known definitions.
cards.quote: It is only in the post-Vedic period that caste became the rigid institution that is familiar to us from well known definitions.

source.book: Indian Society

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Name the six most commonly cited defining features of caste.
cards.back:
Caste is determined by birth
Membership in a caste involves strict rules about marriage.
Caste membership also involves rules about food and food-sharing.
Caste involves a system consisting of many castes arranged in a hierarchy of rank and status.
Castes also involve sub-divisions within themselves
Castes were traditionally linked to occupations.
cards.quote: The most commonly cited defining features of caste are the following:

source.book: Indian Society

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: One can never change one’s caste, leave it, or choose not to join it, although there are instances where a person may be ____ from their caste.
cards.back: One can never change one’s caste, leave it, or choose not to join it, although there are instances where a person may be expelled from their caste.
cards.quote: One can never change one’s caste, leave it, or choose not to join it, although there are instances where a person may be expelled from their caste.

source.book: Indian Society

reasons: review:Blank "expelled" has synonyms (excluded, removed, outcasted); expulsion is a minor exception, low memory value.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What does historical evidence show about caste as an institution?
cards.back: It is also clear from the historical evidence that caste was a very unequal institution – some castes benefitted greatly from the system, while others were condemned to a life of endless labour and subordination.
cards.quote: It is also clear from the historical evidence that caste was a very unequal institution – some castes benefitted greatly from the system, while others were condemned to a life of endless labour and subordination.

source.book: Indian Society

reasons: review:Front is open-ended: historical evidence also shows caste was hereditary and rigid; several answers fit.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Castes that are considered ritually pure have ____ status, while those considered less pure or impure have ____ status.
cards.back: Castes that are considered ritually pure have high status, while those considered less pure or impure have low status.
cards.quote: Castes that are considered ritually pure have high status, while those considered less pure or impure have low status.

source.book: Indian Society

reasons: review:Blanks high/low are inferable from the sentence itself; trivial, adds no memory value.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: On the one hand, the state was committed to the ____ of caste and explicitly wrote this into the Constitution.
cards.back: On the one hand, the state was committed to the abolition of caste and explicitly wrote this into the Constitution.
cards.quote: On the one hand, the state was committed to the abolition of caste and explicitly wrote this into the Constitution.

source.book: Indian Society

reasons: review:Blank "abolition" has obvious synonyms (end, eradication, removal); not a mark-carrying word.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: The only exception to this was in the form of ____ for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
cards.back: The only exception to this was in the form of reservations for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
cards.quote: The only exception to this was in the form of reservations for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

source.book: Indian Society

cards.subject: sociology

cards.back: Modern industry created all kinds of new jobs for which there were no caste rules.
cards.quote: Modern industry created all kinds of new jobs for which there were no caste rules.

source.book: Indian Society

reasons: review:Blank "no caste rules" is open: no caste restrictions, barriers or bars fit equally; not one word.

cards.front: How did recruitment to factory jobs in the mills of Mumbai and Kolkata show the resilience of caste?

cards.quote: The middle men who recruited labour for factories tended to recruit them from their own caste and region so that particular departments or shop floors were often dominated by specific castes.

source.book: Indian Society

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Which castes became the ‘dominant’ castes in the countryside, and with what role?

cards.quote: Their large numbers also gave them political power in the era of electoral democracy based on universal adult franchise.

source.book: Indian Society

cards.subject: sociology

cards.back: The policies of reservation and other forms of protective discrimination instituted by the state in response to political pressure serve as their lifelines.
cards.quote: The policies of reservation and other forms of protective discrimination instituted by the state in response to political pressure serve as their lifelines.

source.book: Indian Society

cards.front: Name the permanent traits by which tribes are classified.

region
language
physical characteristics
ecological habitat

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What share of India's population did tribes form according to Census Report 2011?

cards.quote: This contact itself creates an ideology of “tribalism” – the tribal groups begin to define themselves as tribals in order to distinguish themselves from the newly encountered others.

source.section: Tribe – The Career of a Concept
